github_labels: module: cuda|triaged|module: type promotion|function request|oncall: pt2|module: inductor|module: floatx (formerly float8)|bot-triaged
body_excerpt: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch `tensor.to(dtype)` performs a round-nearest conversion. This makes sense in most cases, but there are situations where other rounding modes are useful. For example in MXFP8 (microscaled float8) on Blackwell GPUs, we need to convert the scales to their next power of 2 and convert them to a float8_e8m0fnu (i.e., a biased uint8). This could be done in one shot via `scales.to(torch.float8_e8m0fnu, round="up")`. Which then would allow PyTorch to match this exactly to the optimized PTX instruction `cvt.rp.satfinite.ue8m0x2.f32` (`.rp` means round-positive). ### Alternatives Several less-readable alternatives, which will also make it harder for PyTorch and Inductor to understand the intent and thus optimize the code. For example one could go through torch.log and torch.ceil, or through torch.frexp, or do the cast with round-nearest and the conditionally adjust the result. ### Additional context _No response_ cc @ptrblck @msaroufim @eqy @jerryzh168 @tinglvv @nWEIdia @nairbv @mruberry @voznesenskym @penguinwu @EikanWang @jgong5 @Guobing-Chen @XiaobingSuper @zhuhaozhe @blzheng @wenzhe-nrv @jiayisunx @ipiszy @kadeng @muchulee8 @amjames @chauhang @aak...

body_excerpt: ## Problem The Relax TFLite frontend currently has two related blockers for quantized TFLite import. First, quantized tensors are blocked early in `get_tensors()` by the tensor quantization metadata guard. After preserving tensor-level quantization metadata (`scale`, `zero_point`, and `axis`) and allowing the frontend to proceed further, the next blocker appears at the operator conversion stage: ```text NameError: name '_qnn' is not defined ``` This happens because the frontend contains quantized operator conversion paths that reference non-existent `_qnn.op.*` APIs. At the same time, Relax already provides `quantize` / `dequantize` operators with C++ registration, Python APIs, legalization to TE, and tests. This suggests that quantized TFLite operators may initially be imported using QDQ decomposition around existing Relax ops, rather than requiring a new set of fused QNN operators as the first step.
